test_title: PYST 39: RRB Group D - Mathematics (Held On: 14 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: A train overtakes two people walking along a railway track. The first person walks at 7.2 km/hr, and the second person walks at 14.4 km/hr. The train takes 29.9 seconds to pass the first person and 43.7 seconds to pass the second person. What is the speed of the train if both are walking in the same direction as the train?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert speeds: 7.2 → 2 m/s, 14.4 → 4 m/s

Use same concept: Length = (v − speed) × time

(v − 2) × 29.9 = (v − 4) × 43.7

Solve ⇒ v = 8.33 m/s

**∴ Answer = 30 km/hr**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of first person = 7.2 km/hr = 2 m/s

Speed of second person = 14.4 km/hr = 4 m/s

Time to pass first person = 29.9 s

Time to pass second person = 43.7 s

**Formula used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Relative speed (same direction) = Train speed − Person speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let speed of train = v m/s

⇒ Length of train = (v − 2) × 29.9

⇒ Length of train = (v − 4) × 43.7

⇒ (v − 2) × 29.9 = (v − 4) × 43.7

⇒ 29.9v − 59.8 = 43.7v − 174.8

⇒ 174.8 − 59.8 = 43.7v − 29.9v

⇒ 115 = 13.8v

⇒ v = 115 ÷ 13.8

⇒ v = 8.33 m/s

⇒ v = 8.33 × 3.6 = 30 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 30 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

Same direction ⇒ Relative speed = Train speed − Person speed

Train Length Formula

Length = Relative speed × Time

Unit Conversion

1 m/s = 3.6 km/hr

Key Strategy

Same train length ⇒ equate both equations to eliminate length
